name: Corinna
reason: Wikivoyage (Arthur-Pieman page) and Parks Tas name the Corinna ferry crossing as the way in; the settlement is a historic Pieman River gateway, but no source I could open lists anything to see or do there (the Wikivoyage Corinna page is empty).
objection: Case for: historic Huon pine settlement, Pieman River cruise and a base for the Tarkine. Against: its draw is access to the Tarkine (the ferry is a vehicle), one real source, visit mostly a stopover; a town is a spot only if it is a draw itself.

name: Hells Gates
reason: Entrance headland to Macquarie Harbour, seen only from Gordon River cruises (Wikivoyage Strahan lists it inside the cruise description); no public place to stand, so rule 2 fails and it is part of the cruise experience.
objection: Strongest case for: Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage both name it and it has 3.7k views. But the visit is a vehicle trip's passing view, and the sightseeing is Macquarie Harbour/Gordon River, not a spot you can do for half an hour.

name: Lake St Clair
reason: Parks & Wildlife Tasmania visitor page (opened) lists a visitor centre, short walks, swimming and the Overland Track end: a lake with things to do, not the Michigan lake of the same name (pin must be the Tasmanian lake near Cynthia Bay, about -42.12, 146.18, not the wiki-sourced coordinates).
objection: Part of the national park and Overland Track spots; may be a near-duplicate if the park is itself a spot. Answer: the lake and its Cynthia Bay hub (cruise, short walks, visitor centre) is a distinct stop reached from the Lyell Highway; page views of 63k are polluted by Michigan so do not use them as evidence.

name: Macquarie Harbour Cruises
reason: An operator and cruise (the vehicle), not a place; the places it goes to (Macquarie Harbour, Sarah Island, Gordon River) are the spots.
objection: Wikivoyage names it first under See in Strahan, but COVERAGE.md 'A spot is a place' rules out operators. Sarah Island/Gordon River should be judged separately.

name: Nelson Falls
reason: Wikivoyage Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers NP (opened) calls it the park's highlight: 30 m fall, 1.4 km return, about 20 minutes boardwalk; also in Wikivoyage Queenstown and Parks Tas Great Short Walks.
objection: About 20 minutes return, a roadside walk on the Lyell Highway, could be a part of the park spot; but it is a named Great Short Walk with three counted sources, a second-tier stop.

name: Overland Track
reason: Parks Tas and Wikivoyage Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair name it as Tasmania's signature multi-day walk (65 km); multi-day walks that agencies promote are explicitly spots (Hump Ridge Track).
objection: Overlaps the national park spot and Lake St Clair (the end point); but a named walk is a distinct draw and the pin goes mid-route. Booking and fees apply, not an objection to inclusion.

name: Queenstown
reason: Wikivoyage Queenstown (opened) lists its own draws: Galley Museum, Douggie's underground mine tours, Spion Kopf and Iron Blow lookouts, the historic streetscape and the mined-hill landscape.
objection: The Railway starts here and the town is a transit stop on the Lyell Highway; but the town has several open attractions of its own, so it passes as a town with its own draws.

name: Rosebery Folk Festival
reason: An annual event, not a permanent place (rule 4).
objection: None of substance: festivals belong in best-time text. Any permanent Rosebery venue would be judged separately.

name: Strahan
reason: Wikivoyage Strahan (opened) and Discover Tasmania: the region's main tourist town, with waterfront, Water Tower Hill Lookout, foreshore walk and Regatta Point; the base for the Gordon River.
objection: Much of what visitors do is cruises and the railway (vehicles) and Hogarth Falls is its own spot; but the waterfront and harbour town itself is a second-tier harbour-town stop, and the guides give it its own page.

name: Tullah
reason: Wikivoyage Tullah (opened) lists Mackintosh Dam (views, 4 km detour) and the Wee Georgie Wood Steam Railway (Oct-Apr weekends, 20-minute rides); the page itself calls the town a quick stopover on the A10.
objection: Case against: a town is a spot only if the town is a draw, and its draws are the dam and a weekend-only railway, which are better as their own spots; case for: a few things to do and two counted sources. Judge Mackintosh Dam and Wee Georgie Wood Railway separately.

name: Zeehan
reason: Wikivoyage Zeehan (opened) lists the West Coast Heritage Centre (daily 9:30-4, a museum of West Coast mining life) and notes the preserved heritage streetscape of the old silver-mining town.
objection: Only one listed See item and a small town; but a one-street heritage mining town with an open museum fills half an hour to an hour, and is a second-tier town stop.
